modelClaim.name: Kling 4.0
modelClaim.sourceTextOriginal:
Just 48 hours ago Kling 4.0 opened to everyone.

These are not real🤯

7 wild examples + PROMPTS:

1. UGC character at brunch

PROMPT: Raw vertical 9:16 video recorded on a phone's front camera (not on screen), one continuous 30-second take with no cuts. It looks like an ordinary unedited phone clip, not a film: slightly soft image, a little digital noise and compression, deep focus with the café behind her as sharp as her face, auto-exposure brightening and dimming as people pass the sunny window behind her, no colour grading. The phone sits close and a little low, looking slightly up at her; around 9 s a waiter's arm bumps the table, the phone slides and tilts, and she catches it and props it back up. Sadie, a young woman in her early 20s with long honey-blonde waves, light natural makeup, small gold hoop earrings and a cropped cream knit top, sits at a small marble table by a big sunny window in a busy brunch café. Her sister sits across from her, out of frame except for her arm and a hand with a silver ring. Behind Sadie: other tables of people talking, a counter with a glass pastry case, plants, staff moving about, chalkboards too far away to read. Around 9 s a waiter sets down two plates, a lemon ricotta pancakes and a plate of eggs on toast, plus two iced coffees in plain glasses. Around 15 s she turns the pancake plate toward the camera; around 20 s she cuts a bite, eats it and closes her eyes; around 26 s her sister's hand reaches in with a fork and steals a piece of pancake, and Sadie swats at it, laughing. [Sadie: casual young woman's voice, warm and a bit giggly, recorded on the phone's built-in mic from half a metre away]: "Okay, I promised I'd show you what we get. ... We get the same thing every single time. ... Oh, here it is! Thank you! ... Look at this. Lemon ricotta pancakes. ... Mmm. Okay. Yeah. Still the best. ... Hey! Get your own!" [Her sister, off camera: a young woman's voice, dry and amused]: "That's the tax." [Sadie, laughing]: "She does this every time." Audio as captured by the phone mic in a busy café, not studio clean: her voice close but with the room around it, the hiss and grind of an espresso machine, cups and cutlery clinking, overlapping chatter and laughter from other tables, a door bell jingling, a chair scraping, faint music in the background. No subtitles, no captions, no on-screen text.

originalPrompt: A 30-second, seven-shot ski film edit of Kai <Character reference> skiing one steep, untracked mountain face at golden hour, cut together from several real cameras: a drone, a helmet-mounted action camera, an action camera on a pole, a camera planted in the snow, a chase skier and a long lens across the valley. Photoreal action-sports look, real speed, hard cuts on the action, no slow motion. Kai: athletic man in his 20s, red insulated ski jacket, black ski pants, black gloves, white helmet, mirrored orange goggles, black poles, twin-tip skis. Same outfit and gear in every shot, exactly as in the character sheet. Same mountain face, same powder, and the low sun always on his left as he skis down, throwing long blue shadows across the snow. Shot 1 (0-4s), drone: high aerial view of a sunlit ridge and the whole golden face below it. Kai, small in frame, drops in off the ridge and carves his first big turn, a plume of powder behind him. The drone pushes forward and tilts down to follow. Hard cut. Shot 2 (4-8s), helmet cam: first-person view from an action camera on his helmet, ultra-wide with curved edges. His ski tips and pole baskets at the bottom of the frame, snow rushing underneath, the horizon tilting hard left and right with each carve, powder spraying across the lens. Hard cut. Shot 3 (8-12s), pole cam: an action camera on a short pole held out in his left hand, ultra-wide, pointing back at him. His goggles and helmet fill one side of the frame, his body leaning into a turn, the mountain and sky swinging behind him, snow flecks stuck to the lens. He lets out a wordless shout into the wind. Hard cut. Shot 4 (12-17s), planted cam: a camera set low in the snow just below a wind-lip, pointing up at the sky. Kai launches off the lip and flies straight over the lens, skis crossing the low sun, snow raining down onto the camera, then he lands out of frame behind it. Hard cut. Shot 5 (17-21s), chase skier: a camera on a handheld stabiliser, skiing a few metres behind him at the same speed. He drops into a tuck and straight-lines the fall line, spray from his tails hitting the lens, the slope streaking past. Hard cut. Shot 6 (21-25s), long lens: a telephoto shot from across the valley, slightly shaky, compressing the slope. Kai lays a huge carve and throws a wall of powder backlit gold by the sun. Hard cut. Shot 7 (25-30s), low static camera at the bottom of the run: he skis straight at the lens and skids a hard hockey stop right in front of it, a sheet of snow blasting the camera. As it clears, he pushes his goggles up onto his helmet, breathing hard and laughing. Look: every action-camera shot ultra-wide and crisp with curved edges, small lens flares and snow on the lens; the drone and long-lens shots clean and natural. Warm low sun, long blue shadows, glittering ice crystals in the spray, natural colour, real motion blur. Sound, in stereo, loud and up front like real action-camera audio, never quiet: constant wind roaring and buffeting the camera mics, gusting harder as he picks up speed; the crunch of snow under his skis as he drops in; friends whooping and yelling "Go!" from the ridge at the start; the hiss, scrape and chatter of his edges biting the snow on every carve; poles planting with a crisp crunch; powder spraying off his tails with a soft roar; his hard breathing, and a grunt on the landing; a loud whoosh and the clack of skis as he flies over the planted camera, then the thud of the landing; distant ravens calling across the valley; the ripping sheet of snow blasting the lens on the hockey stop, then his panting laugh and his friends cheering from up the slope. A driving instrumental track with punchy drums sits low underneath, cut on the beat, never covering the natural sound. No subtitles.
